executive_summary: Sleep quality and duration were the most prominent issue: the week began with excellent rest but quickly devolved into a stretch of 5 straight nights of short, fragmented, or poor sleep, leading to accumulated sleep debt, daytime headaches, and repeated trialing of evening sleep-improvement tactics.

Significant nutrition routine change: on May 7 (Thu), Jukka officially ended his longstanding intermittent fasting habit, opting instead for a calorie-restricted, portion-controlled approach, reflected in both meal timing and content for the rest of the week.

Work was consistently completed during structured 9:00–16:30 blocks (May 5–8), with a notable rhythm of deep, focus-driven coding/personal projects on May 7 and a lighter, computer-focused flow on Saturday May 9.
Wellness micro-habits—hydration, standing, finger stretches—were tracked and consistently maintained (4+ days), even on low-energy or headache-recovery days, suggesting a robust baseline adherence.

Family logistics, caregiving, and pet care were ever-present: mornings and evenings regularly included dog walks (user typically handles evenings), school/admin forms, food duties, and robust family/social rituals (notably, Friday Night Meats on May 8).
Communication and digital organization demands were high—especially on May 8–9—with heavy assistant use for outbound email, calendar management, and family planning.
Recurring household automation and routine interruptions (Ring, light automations) surfaced several times, suggesting systematic reliability issues.

Even with energy constraints, deliberate efforts were made to maintain or improve routines—especially in sleep hygiene (liquid taper, CPAP, early lights-out) and nutrition (GERD-aware meal planning, portion control).
